title: Basil Hayden’s High-Rye Trail
summary: In 1785 Basil Hayden Sr. led twenty-five Maryland Catholic families to Kentucky, where they cleared land and planted crops on claims on Pottinger's Creek.
bodyMarkdown:
In 1785 Basil Hayden Sr. led twenty-five Maryland Catholic families west to Kentucky, seeking land and religious freedom on the frontier. Hayden was born in St. Mary's County, Maryland.

Their route ran by flatboat down the Ohio to Limestone (now Maysville) and overland to Goodwin's Station. Leaving the women and children there, the men went on to their claims on Pottinger's Creek, then in Nelson County and now in [Marion County](https://grokipedia.com/page/Marion_County,_Kentucky). There they cleared land, built homes and planted their first crops.

Faith shaped the settlement as much as farming. Father Charles Whelan arrived in 1787 and said Mass in private homes, including Hayden's. In 1790 Father William de Rohan began a log church on two acres of land provided by Hayden, and it was completed in 1792. The [Kentucky Historical Society's marker](https://history.ky.gov/markers/catholic-pioneers) calls it the first Catholic church west of the Alleghenies; it became known as [Holy Cross](https://grokipedia.com/page/holy_cross_church_(marion_county,_kentucky)), and the present brick church, built in 1823 under Father Charles Nerinckx, also stands on land that Hayden donated.

Hayden also made whiskey. Accounts behind the [Basil Hayden's](https://grokipedia.com/page/Basil_Hayden%27s) brand say that he used a larger share of rye in his corn-based mash than was common. The brand dates that recipe to about 1796, but those details come largely from company and family tradition rather than surviving distilling records.

His name lasted through his descendants. His grandson Raymond B. Hayden created the [Old Grand-Dad](https://grokipedia.com/page/Old_Grand-Dad) label around 1840. In 1992 Booker Noe, a master distiller at [Jim Beam](https://grokipedia.com/page/Jim_Beam) and grandson of its founder, James B. Beam, created Basil Hayden's as a high-rye bourbon for Beam's Small Batch Collection: 63 percent corn, 27 percent rye and 10 percent malted barley, bottled at 80 proof. The Beam family's own early history is told in [Jacob Beam on Hardin Creek](/stories/jacob-beam-on-hardin-creek/).

## Kentucky today

[Holy Cross Church](https://grokipedia.com/page/holy_cross_church_(marion_county,_kentucky)) still stands on Pottinger's Creek in Marion County, its 1823 brick church on land Hayden donated, and a [state historical marker](https://history.ky.gov/markers/catholic-pioneers) honors the Catholic pioneers who settled there. [Basil Hayden's](https://grokipedia.com/page/Basil_Hayden%27s) is distilled at Clermont, not far from the bourbon country around [Bardstown](/stories/bardstown/).
